'''Tsukimoto Shrine''' (槻本神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Takayama City|Takayama City]], {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|en|Gifu Prefecture|qid=Q131277|lt=Gifu Prefecture}}. It is identified as the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} "Tsukimoto Shrine" in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō}} for {{ill|Hida Province|en|Hida Province|qid=Q1056535|lt=Hida Province}}'s {{ill|Ōno District, Gifu|en|Ōno District, Gifu|qid=Q31671|lt=Ōno District (Gifu)}}.

The shrine's sacred cedar tree ({{ill|Cryptomeria|en|Cryptomeria|qid=Q147388|lt=Cryptomeria}}) is designated as a Gifu Prefecture Natural Monument.<ref name="sugi">{{Cite web|language=ja|date= |url=http://www.pref.gifu.lg.jp/kyoiku-bunka-sports/bunka-geijutsu/bunkazai-zuroku/bunkazai-zuroku/tenki/takayamsi/tukimoto.html |title=Tsukimoto Shrine's Cedar Tree |publisher=Gifu Prefecture |accessdate=2013-04-20}}</ref> The tree is estimated to be over 1,200 years old, and local lore warns that those who harm it will quickly fall ill and die.

== History ==
The date of the shrine's founding is unknown. According to legend, the original sacred object was a giant {{ill|Zelkova serrata|en|Zelkova serrata|qid=Q920344|lt=Zelkova}} tree (槻), which continued to exist even after the construction of the shrine buildings. Another version of the legend attributes the sacred status to a giant cedar tree instead of a zelkova.

The current shrine structure was rebuilt in the 5th year of {{ill|Genbun|en|Genbun|qid=Q1145754|lt=Genbun}} (1740). In the 4th year of the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} (1871), the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}.

== Enshrined Deities ==
* [[Ōyama-tsumi|Ōyama-tsumi no Kami]]
* [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Kushimikeno no Kami]]
* [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]]
* [[Yasakatome|Yasakatome no Kami]]

Alternate theories identify the deities as {{ill|Ukemochi|en|Ukemochi|qid=Q2280323|lt=Ukemochi no Kami}} and Tsukimoto Daimyōjin.

== Cultural Properties ==
* **Cedar Tree of Tsukimoto Shrine** - Designated as a Gifu Prefecture Natural Monument.<ref name="sugi" />
* **Monument Inscribed with the Shrine's name** - Designated as a Takayama City Historic Site.<ref>{{Cite web|language=ja|date= |url=http://www.city.takayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/bunkazai/siseki/index.htm |title=Historic Sites and Scenic Spots |publisher=Takayama City |accessdate=2013-04-23}}</ref>

== Access ==
* Approximately 7 km northeast of {{ill|Takayama Station|en|Takayama Station|qid=Q874020|lt=Takayama Station}} on the {{ill|Takayama Main Line|en|Takayama Main Line|qid=Q1188357|lt=Takayama Main Line}}.
** Follow [[:en:National Route 158|National Route 158]] eastward along the Yamaguchi Valley (a tributary of the {{ill|Jinzū River|en|Jinzū River|qid=Q1156518|lt=Miyagawa}}) from Nyūkawa Town, Yamaguchi.
** Alternatively, travel south from National Route 158 in Nyūkawa Town, Bōgata. Pass through the Nyūkawa Tunnel on the Hida Farm Road, then head west for about 1 km.
